title: Vanishing localizations form an ideal
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small ringed site with sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, let $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and for each object $U$ define $S_K(U)=\{f\in\mathcal O(U)\mid R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],K|_U)=0\}$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The assignment $U\mapsto S_K(U)$ is a sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O$: it contains $0$, is closed under multiplication by arbitrary sections, and if $f,g\in S_K(U)$ then $f+g\in S_K(U)$. Consequently, if an ideal sheaf is generated locally by sections $b_1,\ldots,b_r$, every section of that ideal belongs locally to $S_K$ whenever each $b_i$ does. [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]

source.place: Tag 0998 (lemma-ideal-of-elements-complete-wrt), with Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af) identifying its vanishing criterion with derived internal Hom.

proof.text: On the slice over $U$, write $F_f=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],K|_U)$. Localization at zero is the zero module, so $F_0=0$ by the Hom-complex formula. Thus $0\in S_K(U)$.

source.place: Tag 0998 (lemma-ideal-of-elements-complete-wrt), with Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af) identifying its vanishing criterion with derived internal Hom.

proof.text: For $f\in S_K(U)$ and $a\in\mathcal O(U)$ apply the localization internal-Hom identity with $P=\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ and localizing section $a$. It gives $F_{af}\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/a],F_f)=0$. This also applies when either section is zero; in particular $a=-1$ proves closure under negatives.

source.place: Tag 0998 (lemma-ideal-of-elements-complete-wrt), with Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af) identifying its vanishing criterion with derived internal Hom.

proof.text: For $f,g\in S_K(U)$ put $h=f+g$. For each $V\to U$ take $R=\mathcal O(V)[1/h]$. The images of $f,g$ generate its unit ideal because $f/h+g/h=1$. The standard-covering gluing statement gives injectivity and middle exactness of $0\to R\to R[1/f]\oplus R[1/g]\to R[1/(fg)]$, with diagonal and difference maps. For surjectivity, represent an element of the last term as $z/(fg)^n$, increasing $n$ to be positive. The binomial expansion of $(f/h+g/h)^{2n-1}=1$ gives $u f^n+v g^n=1$ for some $u,v\in R$. The pair $(vz/f^n,-uz/g^n)$ maps to $z/(fg)^n$. Sheafifying this sectionwise exact sequence gives $0\to\mathcal O_U[1/h]\to\mathcal O_U[1/(fh)]\oplus\mathcal O_U[1/(gh)]\to\mathcal O_U[1/(fgh)]\to0$; iterated localization agrees with localization at the product by its universal property.

source.place: Tag 0998 (lemma-ideal-of-elements-complete-wrt), with Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af) identifying its vanishing criterion with derived internal Hom.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_U[1/h]$, $B=\mathcal O_U[1/(fh)]\oplus\mathcal O_U[1/(gh)]$, $D=\mathcal O_U[1/(fgh)]$, and let $i:A\to B$ be the injection of step 3. In degree-zero complexes its cone $T=C(i)$ is $A\xrightarrow{i}B$ in degrees $-1,0$. The projection $T\to D[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its degree $-1$ cohomology is $\ker i=0$, and its degree $0$ cohomology is $\operatorname{coker}i=D$. Choose a K-injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $K|_U$, and write $H(X)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(X,I^\bullet)$. The quasi-isomorphism clause of the derived internal-Hom definition gives a quasi-isomorphism $H(D)\to H(T)$. Step 2 gives $F_{fh}=F_{gh}=F_{fgh}=0$ (multipliers $h,h,gh$ respectively), so $H(T)$ and $H(B)=H(\mathcal O_U[1/(fh)])\oplus H(\mathcal O_U[1/(gh)])$ are acyclic. The degreewise split sequence $0\to B\to T\to A[1]\to0$ gives $0\to H(A[1])\to H(T)\to H(B)\to0$, also degreewise split: restriction to the graded summand $B$ is surjective, with kernel the maps factoring through the graded quotient $A[1]$, and the Hom differential preserves this kernel. Its kernel is acyclic by the following local boundary chase. For a closed local section $x$ of the kernel, acyclicity of $H(T)$ gives locally $y$ with $dy=x$; its image $\bar y$ is closed in $H(B)$, so locally $\bar y=dz$. Lift $z$ using the degreewise splitting; then $y-d\widetilde z$ lies in the kernel and has differential $x$. Thus $H(A[1])$ has zero cohomology sheaves. Its degree $n$ term is $\mathcal Hom(A,I^{n-1})$, with the differential of $I$, so its cohomology is that of $H(A)$ shifted by one degree. Therefore $F_h=0$ and $f+g\in S_K(U)$.

source.place: Tag 0998 (lemma-ideal-of-elements-complete-wrt), with Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af) identifying its vanishing criterion with derived internal Hom.

proof.text: For any arrow $V\to U$, the restriction identity for localization internal Hom gives $F_f|_V\cong F_{f|_V}$. Hence membership is preserved by restriction. Conversely, suppose $f|_{U_i}\in S_K(U_i)$ for a covering family of $U$. Then $F_f|_{U_i}=0$ for all $i$. Slice restriction is evaluation of module sheaves on objects lying over $U_i$, so preserves kernels and the locally defined images; it therefore commutes with cohomology. Every cohomology sheaf of $F_f$ restricts to zero on the cover. A section of such a sheaf over any $V\to U$ vanishes on the pulled-back covering sieve and is zero by the uniqueness axiom for a sheaf. Thus all cohomology sheaves vanish, the representative complex is quasi-isomorphic to zero, and $F_f=0$. A compatible family in $S_K$ glues uniquely in $\mathcal O$, and this local criterion puts its glued section in $S_K$. Together with steps 1--4 this proves that $S_K$ is a sheaf of ideals.

source.place: Tag 0998 (lemma-ideal-of-elements-complete-wrt), with Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af) identifying its vanishing criterion with derived internal Hom.

proof.text: On a slice where $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ generate the ideal sheaf and belong to $S_K$, a section of the generated ideal is locally a finite sum $\sum_i a_i b_i$. Step 2 puts each summand in $S_K$, and repeated application of step 4 puts the sum in $S_K$. Step 5 glues the local membership. For $r=0$ the generated ideal is zero and step 1 applies.
